migration.description: Introduce a durable prompt-cache conversation master and compact proxy invocation identity allocation.
migration.release_unit_description: Prompt-cache conversation background materialization follow-up for the conversation and invoke ID redesign.

durable_state.description: Prompt-cache conversation identity rows and delayed aggregate statistics derived from retained proxy invocations, with a durable refresh queue, freshness markers, and resumable phase/cursor state for background materialization.
durable_state.storage_implementation: SQLite prompt_cache_conversations table, prompt_cache_conversation_stats_refresh_queue table, prompt_cache_conversation_migration_progress table, prompt_cache_conversation_materialization_runs table, codex_invocations mutation triggers, startup_backfill_progress with its durable enabled flag, and schema_refresh_migrations markers for identity backfill and aggregate-statistics freshness.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create prompt_cache_conversations, its constraints, and lookup indexes.
Create the durable prompt-cache statistics refresh queue and codex_invocations mutation triggers that enqueue affected keys and invalidate freshness.

Create the additive migration progress table with migration_name, phase, source_max_invocation_id, cursor_key, updated_at, and the durable source total so materialization can resume after cancellation or restart and expose bounded progress.
Create the bounded materialization run history table for phase, duration, processed/updated counts, batch metrics, defer reasons, and failures; retain only the latest 100 rows.

dml_changes.description: In the background identity_backfill phase, snapshot the maximum invocation ID and materialize distinct historical prompt-cache keys by keyset pages; after the snapshot scan, run uncursored missing-identity reconciliation and record the identity marker only after coverage is complete.

In the background stats_rebuild phase, refresh aggregate fields for conversation keys by 400-key logical pages split into adaptive 32..400-key micro-batches; each micro-batch uses one set-based aggregate writeback and commits identity ensure, aggregate refresh, queue clearing, and its durable cursor checkpoint in one transaction after identity coverage is complete.

In the background queue_drain phase, refresh and clear durable mutation-queue keys only after successful aggregate refresh, then record the statistics freshness marker and complete phase when the queue is empty.

progress_signals: The prompt_cache_conversation_migration_progress row exposes the current phase, invocation snapshot boundary, keyset cursor, and updated_at checkpoint.

The system prompt-cache materialization status surface exposes total keys, completed keys, progress, queue backlog, estimated remaining time, the latest 10 bounded run records, and a durable pause/resume control.

Structured startup-backfill logs expose phase, scanned, updated, completion, retry, failure, and defer status, together with micro-batch count, last/max batch size, accumulated batch time, and defer reason.
Structured identity creation, collision retry, database recovery, statistics refresh, and retention release logs.

The prompt_cache_conversations_stats_v2 marker identifies a completed aggregate refresh only when the prompt_cache_conversation_stats_refresh_queue is empty; its absence or a pending queue triggers a paged startup rebuild.
pause_points: Schema installation stops after additive DDL and does not scan historical invocations, allowing HTTP readiness to continue.

The operator control disables the prompt-cache task at the next committed micro-batch boundary and wakes it from its durable cursor when re-enabled; it does not interrupt an active SQLite transaction.

Each 400-key logical page is split into adaptive 32..400-key transactions. A micro-batch runs to commit or explicit failure, and its phase cursor advances in that same transaction; after a committed adaptive batch a 2 ms scheduler window gives foreground readers a bounded opportunity before the next batch. Prompt-cache pressure defers the next boundary while process exit or failure repeats the latest idempotent micro-batch.

SQLite invocation mutation triggers enqueue affected prompt-cache keys and remove the freshness marker in the source transaction; startup recovery can rebuild aggregates and identities after a stopped release.

required_test_evidence: Schema installation completes without scanning historical prompt-cache invocations.
A bounded startup materialization creates identities, checkpoints committed pages, and reruns without duplicate identities.
Adaptive 32..400-key micro-batches keep identity, statistics, queue clearing, and cursor checkpoint work in committed transactions and yield only at boundaries.
A stopped release or process restart resumes from the durable phase/cursor and converges to both markers with an empty queue.
An invocation payload update enqueues its prompt-cache key and startup recovery creates the missing identity before rebuilding aggregates.
Aggregate reads return the existing unavailable contract while identity, statistics, or queue completeness is not satisfied.
A cache miss recovers the next sequence from retained invocation IDs.
Retention releases orphan masters without a permanent ID blacklist.
